$comment: Modules an extracted application also holds, byte for byte.
Each was duplicated rather than moved, and each for a reason recorded in the
extraction that did it:
polyline / activity-meta / track / tile-math — $lib/geo (Landgrab) imports
all four at five sites and Landgrab is deferred, so Main needs them and
Health took them. geo/tiles.ts matches track's haversine 'so distances
agree': if the copies diverge, Landgrab's scoring atom moves and nothing
anywhere fails.
file-store/storage — the boundary linter classifies it PLATFORM and
thirteen non-Drive modules import it, including the public hero video.
Both copies point at one WORKFLOW_FILES_ROOT.
file-shares / file-serving — the share capability is minted by one process
and may be resolved by the other. Divergence is a valid link rejected.
intel/source-policy — the pure half of the folder policy; its DB-aware half
stayed here.
webdav/auth — verifies the Basic credential for a MOUNTED filesystem. Two
live credentials depend on both hooks agreeing, and /dav is still served
from here while Drive holds an identical copy ready.
None of these drifting breaks a build or fails a test. That is exactly why
the hashes are recorded. Change one, change it in the peer repo too, then:
node scripts/record-shared-modules.mjs
apple-health-scale — the x100 that apple_health_metrics.value is stored in.
The ingest that multiplies now lives in SR-Health; the two readers that
divide are here, and both are public: the homepage's step count and the
vitals poll's pulse. A factor that disagreed across the boundary would not
fail a build or log anything, it would just be wrong by a hundred — which
this repo has already shipped once.
health-context-contract — the shape SR-Health's /api/health/context returns
and the chat context panel renders. Types only, so both repos hold it byte
for byte. Redeclaring it instead is how a field starts arriving undefined
with nothing red anywhere.
webdav/paths + propfind + filters — auth.ts was registered and these three
were not, though all four are byte-identical and /dav is still served from
here while SR-Drive holds a copy ready. A path or a PROPFIND response that
disagreed between them is a drive that mounts and then behaves wrongly,
which is worse than one that will not mount at all.
file-index/* — this is a MAIN module that Drive borrowed, not the reverse.
/dav, deepdive/to-drive, intel/mail-admit, knowledge/search, the file-search
workflow node, the file_* agent tools, jkai/media/preanalyse and
/api/jkai/attachments all need it here. If the copies diverge, the same file
indexed by one application is found differently by the other.
store.ts is deliberately NOT here: Drive's copy hands Intelligence a row
instead of importing its engine, which is the whole point of that boundary.
health-sync/* — the Strava and WHOOP INGEST lane, which is ours and stays.
It moved out of $lib/health so that tree can be deleted wholesale once the
dashboard half is gone. SR-Health holds the same five, because /api/health/
sync and the two OAuth callbacks are routed to it, so BOTH applications
refresh the same tokens and write the same tables.
Concurrency is already handled — readOrRefreshToken takes
pg_advisory_xact_lock and re-reads inside the transaction. Divergence is
not: `refreshToken: newTokens.refresh_token || token.refreshToken` is
WHOOP's rotation, and if one repo changes that line both connectors die
with nothing red anywhere.
scheduler.ts is NOT here. It is ours alone — the timer must run exactly
once — and SR-Health's copy is dead code being deleted rather than guarded.
planner-sports — the sports SR-Health's planner accepts and the cap ORS puts
on a round trip. The route_plan tool builds its `sport` enum and its
distance wording from them when the tool registry LOADS, which cannot wait
on another process. Drift offers the model a sport Health rejects, and a
400 inside a tool call reads to a model as a broken route service rather
than a bad argument.
